title: King Janaka keeps his crown
word: reading the Isha in the original
hookLine: a king who stays free while ruling, and the Isha's verse on action
carry: act fully; action without clinging doesn't bind
tomorrow: after a verse about a long life, why does the Isha turn so dark?

lines: QUIT EVERYTHING. MOVE TO A CABIN.
cards: Every so often a video goes around: someone quits everything and moves to a cabin with no signal, and the comments fill up with people wishing they could too. It's a real pull, especially in a heavy week.
Hindu tradition knows that pull well; it honors the forest sage. But it also keeps a story about a man who never left. His name is Janaka, king of Mithila.

teach.h: JANAKA: A SAGE ON A THRONE.
teach.b: Janaka ruled a whole kingdom, with courts and taxes and quarrels, and the old texts still remember him as a knower, a sage on a throne. The Gita names him: Janaka and others reached perfection through action.

The Mahabharata keeps a saying of his: if Mithila is burning, nothing of mine burns. Many teachers read that not as a king who didn't care, since he ruled his city, but as one who didn't hold it as mine.
Now the Isha's second verse: kurvann eveha karmani jijivishet shatam samah.
Doing works, just here, may one wish to live a hundred years. Here, iha, is hidden inside eveha, where eva and iha melt into one sound. Just here.
The second line gives the reason: na karma lipyate nare. Action is not smeared on a person. Here's the teaching.

teach.h: KARMA YOGA: ACTION THAT DOESN'T BIND.
teach.b: This is karma yoga, the path of action, the one the Gita builds on. Karma, the law that actions bind and bear fruit, binds through clinging.
Act fully, offer the work, don't cling to how it turns out, and the action doesn't stick. The Gita uses the same word, lipyate, for it: like water on a lotus leaf.
That's why Hinduism has always had room for the householder, the parent, the king, not only the monk. For a heavy week, that's a different answer from the cabin.

how: Hindu teachers often pair this verse with the Gita's karma yoga: work offered to the Lord, without clinging to its fruits, is said not to bind, which is why the householder's life is honored as a path to freedom.

games.q: what does “reading the isha in the original” mean?
o: the Isha's rules for a hundred years of ritual
a call to leave work and live alone in the forest
a king who ruled and stayed free: action that doesn't bind

games.q: verse two, unglued — tap the pairs.

s: the Isha tells seekers to quit work and go off alone
verse two says doing works, just here, may one wish to live.
the Gita names King Janaka as reaching perfection through action
a king and householder, not a monk.
in Hindu teaching, only those who leave the world can be free
karma yoga: action without clinging doesn't bind, Janaka's path.

games.q: a friend who's burned out says the wise move is to drop every commitment and disappear for a while. what does Isha 2 put on the table?
o: disappear; the verse praises a life with no works at all.
keep doing, just here, in a way the work doesn't stick to you.
work harder; the verse says long life comes from more works.
games.why: kurvann eveha karmani: doing works, just here. like Janaka on his throne, the promise isn't fewer works but that action without clinging doesn't bind.

practice: Rest both hands, palms up, on your lap, and notice them: the hands that did today's work. On each out-breath, let what they've done roll off like water off a lotus leaf, while the hands stay warm and ready.
If you pray, do what many Hindus do at the end of work or worship: offer it, with a simple Krishnarpanam, to Krishna I offer it. If you don't, just let the day's work go.

wordCard.voice: Reading the Isha in the original, verse two: kurvann eveha, doing, just here, and na karma lipyate, action is not smeared on a person. Janaka's verse.

orig.note: Sanskrit, in Devanagari: jijivishet, may one wish to live, from jiv, to live, with wanting folded in.

carryVoice: Your line: act fully; action without clinging doesn't bind. Janaka stayed, and stayed free. Back tomorrow.
